body_markdown:
The European Commission proposed Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) in 2020 to strengthen the operational resilience of EU financial entities and their ICT supply chains, including non-EU providers. Since January 2025, firms must comply, but DORA is about more than compliance: firms must withstand, respond to and recover from ICT disruption. Our new report,


[The Top Five DORA Priorities For 2026 And Beyond](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-top-five-dora-priorities-for-2026-and-beyond/RES203454?ref_search=3540440_1794898870369) (Forrester clients only), examines what leaders should prioritize as DORA moves into active supervision and enforcement.


**Five Areas Where Financial Institutions Continue To Face Challenges**


More than one year in, financial entities impacted by DORA have made progress implementing DORA, although timelines have slipped, budgets swelled up to 10 times the original estimates, and talent shortages continued to hinder sustained compliance. From speaking to organizations undergoing the preparation and execution, we identified five priorities that firms must address when supervisors come knocking, and as they continue to strengthen their operational resilience:


- **Keep DORA controls current.** Technology environments, suppliers, and business services change constantly. Make sure your resilience controls and ICT risk frameworks change with them.


- **Gain visibility into your critical services.** Fragmented supplier data, outdated dependency maps, and complex subcontractor relationships make it difficult to see how disruption could affect critical services. Identify the ICT providers and subcontractors that support each critical service, and keep those dependencies current as providers and services change.


- **Test based on resilience risk.** Limited resources and incomplete dependency information can lead firms to test what they have the capacity for rather than the scenarios and services that pose the greatest resilience risk. Prioritize testing based on resilience risk, using critical service dependencies and plausible disruption scenarios to determine where testing will provide the greatest insights.


- **Prove that exit plans work.** Documenting an exit strategy for a critical ICT provider is not enough, you need to ensure that you can execute all parts of it including the support and data portability. Name a replacement for each of your critical providers, and test data extraction, service migration and the handover to a replacement provider.


- **Map service dependencies and keep them updated.** Firms need a reliable view of the applications, data, infrastructure, and third parties that support critical business services as those dependencies change. Establish end-to-end dependency maps for critical business services and update them whenever the underlying technology or third-party environment changes.


- **Compliance was never supposed to be the end state.** DORA requires financial entities to demonstrate the ability to withstand, respond to and recover from serious ICT disruption. You can either tick the box, or maximize your investment in time, effort and resources to achieve sustainable resilience for your organization.
